title: Government's Proper Role
summary: Government as an agent that protects rights, limited to retaliatory force.

lessons.title: An agent, not a master
lessons.objective: Identify government as an agent that acts for people, not as an owner of their lives.

exercises.prompt: In this unit, what kind of thing is government?

choices.text: An agent that acts for the people whose rights it protects
The owner of the lives and property of its citizens
A private club with no special relation to force
A mood shared by a nation, not an institution

feedback.note: Government is an agent. It does not own the people it serves.

exercises.prompt: An agent acts on whose behalf?

choices.text: The people whose rights it is hired to protect
Only its own officials, as a purpose in themselves
History, which chooses rulers without a job description
Nobody; an agent has no principal

feedback.note: Calling government an agent means it has a principal: the people whose rights it protects.

exercises.prompt: Match each picture of government to the idea it expresses.

pairs.right: Acts for others under a limited job
Treats citizens as subjects it owns
Protect rights, and only by retaliatory force

feedback.note: The proper role is the agent's job: protect rights, and stay inside retaliatory force.

exercises.prompt: Complete the unit's description of government.

feedback.note: The word for its standing is agent: it acts for people, under a defined job.

exercises.prompt: Which claim fits an agent and rejects a master?

choices.text: Officials hold a job with a limit, not a blank permission to rule
Once chosen, officials may do anything they judge good
Office is a personal right to command
There is no difference between an agent and a master

feedback.note: An agent is bound by the job. A master is not. This unit keeps government on the agent side.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that states government's standing.

feedback.note: Government is an agent. It is not a sovereign that stands above the rights it is supposed to guard.

exercises.prompt: Match who holds the role to what that role may do.

pairs.right: Carry out the job of protecting rights
Remain the person whose rights are protected
Stop the agent at retaliatory force

feedback.note: The citizen is not the property of the agent. The agent's reach stops at retaliatory force.

exercises.prompt: Finish the contrast.

parts.text: Government is an agent, not a

feedback.note: Master is the rejected picture. Agent is the one this unit teaches.

exercises.prompt: If government is an agent, what follows about its powers?

choices.text: They are limited to the job it was given
They grow whenever officials want a new project
An agent may use no force of any kind
The job is whatever is not written down

feedback.note: An agent's powers track the job. Here the job is protecting rights, and the means stop at retaliatory force.

lessons.title: The job: protect rights
lessons.objective: State the purpose of government as the protection of individual rights, and reject substitute purposes.

exercises.prompt: What is government's job in this unit?

choices.text: Protect individual rights
Decide how wealth should be shared
Force people to be virtuous
Set the nation's tastes and opinions

feedback.note: The purpose named here is protection of rights. Other social projects are not that job.

exercises.prompt: Whose rights does the agent protect?

choices.text: The rights of individuals
Only the rights of people in office
A group right that replaces the individual
No one's; rights are outside politics

feedback.note: The agent protects individual rights. It does not replace the individual with a group that has no rights of its own.

exercises.prompt: Match each proposed purpose to whether it is the job.

pairs.left: Start force for a social plan

feedback.note: Protecting rights is the purpose. Directing lives, or starting force for a plan, is not that purpose.

exercises.prompt: Complete the purpose.

feedback.note: The object of protection is rights. That is the purpose this unit assigns to the agent.

exercises.prompt: A program orders people to give up property so officials can fund a favorite project. What is wrong with it under this unit?

choices.text: It replaces protection of rights with a different purpose
It is fine if the paperwork is slow
A vote makes any purpose the proper role
Only large projects can protect rights

feedback.note: The proper purpose is protecting rights. Taking them for a favorite project is a different purpose.

exercises.prompt: Build the sentence that names the job.

feedback.note: The agent protects rights. It does not invent a new set of duties and call that the same job.

exercises.prompt: Match the phrase to its place in the unit.

pairs.right: How far its force may go

feedback.note: Three pieces stay distinct: what government is, what it is for, and the limit on its force.

exercises.prompt: Fill both parts of the purpose line.

feedback.note: Keep both words: agent, and rights. Drop either one and the purpose is no longer the one in this unit.

exercises.prompt: Which goal still counts as the proper purpose?

choices.text: Stop others from violating a person's rights
Shape a citizen into an official ideal
Pick winners in peaceful trade
Silence ideas officials dislike

feedback.note: Guarding a person against rights-violations is the job. Shaping, picking winners, or silencing is not protection of rights.

lessons.title: Only retaliatory force
lessons.objective: Limit the force government may use to retaliation against those who have started force.

exercises.prompt: What kind of force is government limited to?

choices.text: Retaliatory force
Any force that might improve society
The first use of force, so others will obey
No force, including defense against attackers

feedback.note: The limit is retaliatory force. That includes answering force that was started by someone else. It does not include starting force.

exercises.prompt: Retaliatory force answers what?

choices.text: Force that someone else has already started
A private taste the majority dislikes
The mere fact that someone has less money
Peaceful refusal to join a plan

feedback.note: Retaliation is a response to initiated force. Disagreement, poverty, or a peaceful no is not that trigger.

exercises.prompt: Match each use of force to its place under the limit.

pairs.left: Arrest someone who has committed assault
Seize a peaceful person's goods for a plan

feedback.note: Answering assault or invasion stays inside retaliatory force. Starting force against the peaceful does not.

exercises.prompt: Complete the limit.

feedback.note: The adjective that marks the limit is retaliatory. Unlimited or initiatory force is the thing the limit rules out.

exercises.prompt: Officials threaten fines to make a peaceful speaker stop. Under this unit, that threat is what?

choices.text: A start of force, outside the retaliatory limit
Retaliation, because speech annoyed someone
The job of protecting rights
Not force, because no one was struck

feedback.note: A threat of penalties against a peaceful person is started force. The retaliatory limit does not cover it.

exercises.prompt: Build the limit in one line.

feedback.note: The force government uses must stay retaliatory. Being first to use force is the line it may not cross.

exercises.prompt: Match the word to its meaning in this lesson.

pairs.right: Be the one who starts force
Bar government from the second of those

feedback.note: The limit allows retaliation and bars initiation. Those are not two names for the same act.

exercises.prompt: Fill the contrast.

parts.text: Retaliatory force answers initiated force. It does not

feedback.note: The barred act is to start force. Naming, studying, or trading is not the contrast this lesson draws.

exercises.prompt: Why is retaliatory force still a use of force?

choices.text: It uses force, but only to answer force already started
It is only a speech, never physical
It is the same act as starting force
This unit bans every use of force, including defense

feedback.note: The limit is not pacifism. Government may use force, and only as retaliation.

lessons.title: Police, courts, defense
lessons.objective: Place police, law courts, and armed defense inside the job of protecting rights by retaliatory force.

exercises.prompt: Which set belongs to the proper role?

choices.text: Police, law courts, and armed defense
A state press, a state church, and a state shop
A planning board for every trade
Censors for art, speech, and science

feedback.note: Police, courts, and armed defense are how an agent protects rights with retaliatory force. Running speech, trade, or worship is not.

exercises.prompt: What do the police do when they stay inside the role?

choices.text: Answer crimes that violate rights
Pick which peaceful businesses may open
Edit what people may say
Punish unpopular but peaceful tastes

feedback.note: Police work that belongs here is a response to rights-violations, not direction of peaceful life.

exercises.prompt: Match each function to the retaliatory task it performs.

pairs.right: Answer force and fraud against rights at home
Repel force from outside the country

feedback.note: Each function is a way of protecting rights. None of them is a license to start force against the peaceful.

exercises.prompt: Name the three functions.

feedback.note: Courts and defense sit with the police. Censors and cartels are not functions of this role.

exercises.prompt: Why do courts belong in the proper role?

choices.text: They decide claims of rights under rules, instead of private revenge
They tell people which fashions are moral
They set every price in the market
They require a single faith

feedback.note: Courts are part of retaliatory protection: they settle rights-claims by objective rules rather than by whoever is stronger.

exercises.prompt: Build the list of proper functions.

feedback.note: Police, courts, and defense are the functions that carry out protection by retaliatory force.

exercises.prompt: Match the institution to what would push it outside the role.

pairs.left: A court that ignores rights and obeys a faction
An army used to conquer peaceful neighbors

feedback.note: The same institutions leave the proper role when they start force or stop protecting rights.

exercises.prompt: Complete the link to the limit.

parts.text: These functions use force only as

feedback.note: Police, courts, and defense stay proper only while their force is retaliation in defense of rights.

exercises.prompt: Armed defense fits the unit when it does what?

choices.text: Repels force directed against the rights of the people
Seizes land because it would be useful
Spreads a creed by conquest
Replaces voluntary trade with occupation

feedback.note: Defense is retaliatory when it answers force. Conquest for land, creed, or trade is initiation.

lessons.title: Where the role stops
lessons.objective: Apply the whole unit: an agent that protects rights and stops where retaliatory force stops.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence states the whole unit?

choices.text: Government is an agent that protects rights, limited to retaliatory force
Government may pursue any goal the voters like
Government should not exist in any form
Government owns rights and lends them back

feedback.note: Agent, protection of rights, and the retaliatory limit are one role, not three optional slogans.

exercises.prompt: A law bans a peaceful trade because officials dislike it. Where does it fall?

choices.text: Over the line: it starts force instead of retaliating
On the line: dislike is the same as a rights-violation
Inside the role, because an agent may ban anything
A court function, because a paper was filed

feedback.note: Banning peaceful trade starts force. The role stops before that line.

exercises.prompt: Match each case to the verdict under this unit.

pairs.left: Funding a project by seizing peaceful earnings
A court enforcing a voluntary contract

feedback.note: Answering theft and enforcing a voluntary contract protect rights. Seizing peaceful earnings does not.

exercises.prompt: Restate the summary.

parts.text: An agent that protects rights, limited to

feedback.note: Popularity, totality, or a wish to moralize people does not replace the word retaliatory.

exercises.prompt: What does the limit rule out even when a goal sounds kind?

choices.text: Starting force against people who have not started it
Any private act of kindness
Argument that uses no force
Guarding a victim against an attacker

feedback.note: A kind-sounding goal does not license initiated force. Guarding a victim is still inside retaliation.

exercises.prompt: Build the closing line of the unit.

feedback.note: The close of the unit is protect rights by retaliation only. A decree to do anything is the rejected alternative.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece so the role stays whole.

pairs.left: If it is not an agent
pairs.right: It claims to own the people

pairs.left: If it does not protect rights
If its force is not retaliatory

feedback.note: Drop any one piece and the proper role is gone: the standing, the job, or the limit on force.

exercises.prompt: Fill the two boundaries.

feedback.note: Rights name the job. Retaliation names where the means stop. Tastes and conquest are the decoys.

exercises.prompt: A neighbor asks the government to stop a mugging, and also to stop a rival's honest shop. What may the agent do?

choices.text: Act against the mugging, and refuse to shut the honest shop
Do both, because both requests came from a citizen
Shut the shop only, because trade is easier to police
Do neither, because all force is forbidden

feedback.note: Stopping a mugging is retaliatory protection of rights. Closing an honest shop would start force, so the agent must refuse it.

exercises.prompt: Which change would end the proper role while keeping the same buildings and uniforms?

choices.text: Using those institutions to start force for goals other than rights
Painting the buildings a new color
Giving the police a new official name
Drawing a new map of court districts

feedback.note: Names and buildings do not make the role. Starting force for some other goal leaves the role even if the uniforms stay.
